title: Functions
description: def, parameters, return values, and closures
theory:
### Methods, static versus instance behavior
Java organizes behavior in classes. Instance methods receive a hidden `this` reference; `static` methods belong to the type and cannot access instance fields without an explicit instance.

Methods support overloading: the compiler picks the most specific applicable signature. Overriding replaces inherited behavior when a subclass provides a method with the same signature; annotate overrides with `@Override` to catch signature drift at compile time.

### Lambdas and method references
Functional interfaces (one abstract method) are the target type for lambda expressions and method references. Keep lambdas short; if they grow multi-step logic, use a named private method.

```java
List<String> names = List.of("ada", "bob");
List<String> upper = names.stream()
    .map(String::toUpperCase)
    .toList(); // Java 16+ unmodifiable list from stream
```

exercises.title: Basic Function
exercises.description: Create a function greet() that System.out.printlns Hello. Call it in main.

exercises.title: Function with Parameters
exercises.description: Create function greet(name string) that System.out.printlns Hello, name. Call with "Alice".
hints: Method signature `static void greet(String name)` — use `System.out.println("Hello, " + name);`.

exercises.title: Function with Return
exercises.description: Create function add(a, b int) int that returns a+b. Call with 3 and 4, System.out.println result.
hints: Return `a + b` from `static int add(int a, int b)`.

exercises.title: Multiple Return Values
exercises.description: Create function divide(a, b int) (int, error) that returns quotient and nil error, or 0 and error if b is 0. Call with 10 and 3, System.out.println result and error.
exercises.starter_code: public class Main { static Integer divide(int a,int b){return null;} public static void main(String[] a){} }
hints: The sample returns `Integer` — return `null` when `b == 0`, else `a / b`.
Print `divide(10,3)` and a second call showing `null` for the zero divisor, e.g. `System.out.println(divide(10, 3) + " " + divide(10, 0));`.

exercises.title: Variadic Function
exercises.description: Create function sum(numbers ...int) int that sums all numbers. Call with 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and System.out.println the result.
hints: Use `static int sumAll(int... nums)` and an enhanced `for` to accumulate.

exercises.title: Defer Statement
exercises.description: Create a function process() that System.out.printlns "start", defers System.out.printlning "end", and System.out.printlns "working". Call it in main.
hints: `defer` maps to `try { ... } finally { System.out.println("end"); }` so `"end"` prints after `"working"`.

exercises.title: Closure
exercises.description: Create function makeAdder() that returns a function that adds to a running total. Create adder = makeAdder(), then call adder(5) and adder(10), System.out.printlning both results.
hints: Capture mutable state with `final int[] total = {0};` and return `x -> { total[0] += x; return total[0]; }` as `IntUnaryOperator`.
